t: Process GPT Lite tutorial
h: What you'll do in this tutorial
x: A hands-on guide you follow one step at a time. You start with your first conversation with an AI assistant, then handle documents and tools by chat, cut down repeated work with skills and schedules, share work with teammates, and finally watch ad hoc work become an official company process. What you'll do in this tutorial Process GPT Lite is an AI work assistant you work with through a single conversation . It doesn't stop at answering questions. It creates and edits documents, operates a browser for you, reads your mail and suggests to-dos, hands work over to teammates, and joins meetings to show materials. The execution engine, agents and storage are the open-source Process GPT backend as is. Lite puts a lightweight screen on top of it. This tutorial doesn't list features one by one. It follows how one company's work evolves . Character Role Jinyoung Jang Proposal team lead at a space design company. This is the person you play in this tutorial Minji Kim Designer. Handles floor plans and proposal visuals Seoyeon Park Finance. Reviews quotes and costs Yuki Sato Lighting designer at a partner studio in Tokyo. Writes and speaks Japanese (Chapters 15–16) Moonlight Coffee Customer. Asks by email for a store design proposal and quote for Store #2 The story starts with one email: "Please send us a proposal and a quote for Moonlight Coffee Store #2." On your own, with the AI assistant — At first, Jinyoung asks the assistant questions, has it look things up, and has it sort through mail. Conversations split by topic on their own. Documents and tools too — The assistant makes a floor plan (CAD), a proposal (Word) and a quote (Excel), and edits them right inside the open editor. After editing, it checks on its own that the result matches what you meant. Less repetition — When similar requests arrive every week, you save the approach that worked as a skill , and build a scheduled mission that runs at a set time and a panel app the team shares. As a team — You share outputs with Minji Kim and Seoyeon Park, hand work over with @mentions, and polish it together in the messenger and online meetings. With Yuki Sato, who works in Japanese, messages are translated and meetings are interpreted. What's said in a meeting is saved in the room automatically. As a process — Once the same flow keeps repeating, process mining finds the pattern "receive email → drawing, proposal, quote → finance review → reply" and suggests it to the administrator. After it's registered as an official process, a new request email starts the process on its own, and each step gets an assignee and an agent. Process improvement — After the official process runs for a few months, records pile up. You find which step loses time (bottleneck), whether the work goes into actual working time or waiting time (value stream), and which steps decide the total duration (constraints and the critical path). Then you calculate an improvement in advance, change the process and compare before and after. Extending and operating — You look at the Workroom where Claude Code and Codex work, the system architecture, and operations and security. By the end, you'll be able to take one new customer request all the way from mail → outputs → team review → meeting → official process, and use the records it leaves to make that process faster. Learning path 0 · Getting started Installation, first login, a tour of the screen 1 · You and your AI assistant First conversation, conversation context, mail assistant, browser agent and the Vault 2 · Documents and tools IeumOffice, ArtCraft, from one email to a floor plan, proposal and quote 3 · Less repetition Skills, external connections and scheduled missions, panel apps 4 · Working as a team Shared folders, sharing outputs and @mentions, messenger and translation, online meetings with interpretation 5 · Working in processes Create a process by chat, run it, process mining 6 · Improving processes Find bottlenecks, value streams and the theory of constraint

t: Conversation context — conversations that split on their own, and the output stack
h: Why conversations should split on their own
Try it 1 — mix topics as you talk
Try it 2 — view just one conversation from the list
x: In one chat window, alternate between Moonlight Coffee work and planning the year-end party, and watch the assistant split the conversation by working out, for each message, which story it follows up on. Then pick a single conversation from the conversation list, and expand and open the output stack where the files made in that conversation pile up. Why conversations should split on their own In Chapter 3, you only talked about Moonlight Coffee. But real work doesn't arrive one thing at a time. You look up venues for the year-end party while editing the Moonlight Coffee checklist, then come back to the Moonlight Coffee schedule. In a typical AI chat, you'd have to do one of two things. Make a new chat room yourself for each topic and pick the right one as you go — it's tedious, and easy to pick the wrong room. Mix everything in one room — the assistant gets confused about which one "that checklist" is, and things are hard to find later. Process GPT Lite takes a third path. It keeps one chat window , and each time a message comes in, the context router in front of the assistant (a component that sends a message to the right conversation) decides "which story does this follow up on, or is it a new topic?" and sends it to that conversation. You just talk, and the assistant does the sorting. The router must be connected The current install bundle leaves out the context router and the routing model, so ask your operator to connect them before you follow this chapter ( Chapter 1 ). On a server without them, every message continues in a single conversation, and the N conversations bar and the output stack in this chapter don't appear. How it decides The router takes your recent conversations (their titles and summaries) as candidates and picks which one the new message follows up on. Stage What it does Narrow the candidates Even with many conversations, it passes no more than 6 to the routing model. It always keeps the two most recent conversations, and picks the rest by how much they share words with the message or how close they are in meaning Small routing model A fast, cheap, dedicated routing model chooses first ("routing model" on the line above the answer) Ask a bigger model again If the routing model isn't sure, it asks the default AI model again and measures confidence from the probability of that answer ("routing model→logprob") Stay put if unsure If confidence is below the threshold, it doesn't move the message and stays in the conversation you were in The decision shows on the small line above the answer. What you see Meaning ↳ New topic · (title) A new conversation was started ↳ (title) It was added to the conversation with that title routing model 1.00 The routing model chose it, with confidence 1.00 (the maximum) routing model→logprob 0.99 The routing model hesitated and asked the default AI model again, with confidence 0.99 Directly in the conversation 1.00 You sent it from inside the conversation, so it went there without a decision (Try it 2 below) (nothing) When there's no particular basis for the choice (such as the first message), the mark is left out A conversation's title is the start of the message that began it. So when you bring something up for the first time, say what it's about at the start , like "Moonlight Coffee…" or "Company year-end party…", and it's easy to recognize in the list. Try it 1 — mix topics as you talk In Chapter 3 , you made a Moonlight Coffee conversation. Now you slip in other work and come back. The Vault — where secrets live, and how
x: Hand the assistant work on sites that need a login. You watch the assistant operate a browser in real time, check its plan, and take over to type yourself when needed. You'll also see that the Vault holds passwords, card numbers and verification codes so the AI model never sees them, and how two layers of keys protect them. Why a browser agent The assistant could read the mail in Chapter 5 right away. But issuing a tax invoice on a client portal, checking order history on a supplies site, or changing settings in an admin console can only be done in a logged-in browser , because there's no channel for programs to connect directly. The browser agent operates a browser on the server for you. It reads pages, clicks, types and sums up the results. Two worries come up. Is it safe to give my password to the AI? And what if the AI pays for something on its own? Process GPT Lite answers like this. Worry Safeguard Passwords and card numbers reach the AI The Vault holds the values, and the server types them in itself. The model can only say "put the password here" Secrets get caught in screenshots Secret field values are erased from the page content the model sees, and secret fields are blacked out in screenshots. An open document is linked to the conversation, so the changes you type in chat are applied to the document on screen right away. You'll practice pointing at tables, cell ranges and pictures as you talk, using the dial on the maximized screen, and saving to keep an edited copy. Why open it "right there" In Chapter 3, clicking the checklist Word file card opened an editor inside the screen. In this chapter, the first of Part 2, you learn how to edit documents in that editor by chatting. In a typical AI chat, you download the document the AI made, open it in Hangul or Excel, go back to the AI window to explain what needs fixing, and download yet another new file. The files pile up, and it gets hard to tell which one is the latest. Process GPT Lite opens documents in their original format in an editor next to the chat. The editor is the open-source IeumOffice , and it handles Hangul (HWP/HWPX — the Hangul word processor format widely used in Korea), Word (docx), Excel (xlsx), PowerPoint (pptx) and PDF. The critical path — the chain that sets the total duration In Chapter 21 you found the constraint (Finance review) and candidates for improvement. In this chapter you'll see which steps set the total duration, calculate the candidates in advance, and then actually apply one. A process has steps that run at the same time. In the Moonlight Coffee proposal , once the request is received, Draw floor plan (Minji Kim) and Draft quote (quote agent) start together, and both must finish before it moves on to Write proposal. Even if Draft quote finishes in 3 minutes, Write proposal waits for the floor plan. The total duration is set by the chain that takes the longest . That chain is the critical path . If a step on the critical path is an hour late, the whole thing is an hour late; a step off the critical path can be a little late without affecting the whole. The way to calculate this is the critical path method (CPM). It counts four times for each step. Time Meaning Example: Draft quote ES earliest start The earliest a step can start, once all the steps before it are done 11s (right after the request is received) EF earliest finish ES + step time 3 min LS latest start The latest a step can start without delaying the whole 4.2 hrs LF latest finish The latest a step must finish without delaying the whole 4.2 hrs (when the floor plan finishes) Slack (float) = LS − ES. Installation Q. Do I really need Docker? Yes. The install bundle runs every part with Docker Compose. It works on macOS, Linux and Windows (WSL2). On Windows, we recommend installing Docker Engine inside WSL2 ( Chapter 1 ). Q. The first installation takes too long. The first time, it builds the images itself, which takes 20–40 minutes (the IeumOffice editor takes the longest). From the second time on, it uses the cache and is fast. To use prebuilt images, put LITE_IMAGE_PREFIX and LITE_TAG in .env and it downloads them instead of building. If the build fails for lack of memory, raise Docker's memory to 8GB or more. ArtCraft ( --with-craft ) pulls a prebuilt image, so it doesn't add build time. Q. Which profile should I choose? At first, the default lite is enough. Parts 1–4 (on your own, documents, less repetition, team) all work. To run the processes in Part 5, add ./install.sh --profile full , and to get process suggestions from repeated work, add --with-mining . Q. I installed it, but a feature from one of the chapters doesn't show up. Some things aren't included in the install bundle by default. Feature Why How to turn it on Conversations split by topic ( Chapter 4 ) The routing model uses a GPU or a lot of memory Run the context router separately and set CONTEXT_ROUTER_URL The "related people" order in @teammate suggestions The same routing model JUDGE_URL (without it, only the order of who you talk with most) Editors for drawings, pictures, sound and video ( Chapter 8 ) The image is large (about 660MB) ./install.sh --with-craft (pulls a prebuilt image). Without it, those files open as links, and mail drafts come with only the proposal and quote, no floor plan Claude Code and Codex Workroom ( Chapter 23 ) Needs your own subscription login and the CLI on the host Installed separately Meeting transcription ( Chapter 16 ) Needs a separate speech recognition key TRANSCRIBE_API_KEY Q. How do I let people connect from other PCs? Change .env to PUBLIC_URL=http://<this PC's IP>:18080 and LITE_BIND=0.0.0.0 , set up SMTP, and run ./install.sh again. When you open it to the internet, put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front, and always turn off demo login ( DEMO_LOGIN=0 ). Q. The login code email doesn't arrive. If you haven't set up SMTP, the code goes not to a real mailbox but to the mailbox included in the installation, http://localhost:18025 . If it's not there either, look at docker compose logs auth . Keys and cost Q. Which keys do I need? Just one set: the address, key and model name of an OpenAI-compatible API ( LLM_BASE_URL , LLM_API_KEY , LLM_MODEL ). It doesn't have to be OpenAI. An in-house model server or another provider called the same way also works. For online meeting transcription you also need a speech recognition key ( TRANSCRIBE_API_KEY ), and for Google login and Gmail connection you need the login client details registered with Google ( GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID , GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET ). Q. Is there a usage fee? Process GPT Lite itself is open source under the MIT license, so there's no usage fee. The cost is the LLM call charges . If you use an in-house model server, you pay only for that. Q. Which model is called, and when?
